subject: Service accounts, SSO & IP guardrails — HelixHealth onboarding
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tara Singh <tara@helixhealth.com>, HelixHealth DevOps <devops@helixhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: HelixHealth onboarding — access controls kickoff

Hi team,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the PO. Attached is the high-level onboarding plan I promised (helix_onboard_ma_plan.pdf). Primary goals for our kickoff:

- Confirm SSO/SAML flow and desired IdP attributes (email, groups, employee_id).
- Agree SCIM scope and which AD groups map to Redwood roles.
- Determine IP allowlist ranges for staging and prod; clarify change window.
- Define service-account ownership and delegation model for integrations.
- Capture org-level policies: session timeout, role review cadence, audit log retention.

Jordan — can you lead the service-account pattern discussion and provide a recommended roster template? Ben — please own the IP allowlist cadence and any network exceptions. Tara / DevOps — if you can share the current IdP & SCIM contact and sample metadata (IdP metadata xml, provisioning token) before Tuesday, that will speed things up.

Proposed week-of-11/22: split cadence — implementation workshop (technical) + executive signoff (policy). I listed proposed owners in the attached.

Ask: Tara, can you confirm whether HelixHealth will require an on-prem HSM or key vault integration for signing artifacts?

Thanks,
Monica

--
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0123
From: Tara Singh <tara@helixhealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: HelixHealth DevOps <devops@helixhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: HelixHealth onboarding — access controls kickoff

Hi Monica — thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers:

- We use Okta as our IdP; I attached the IdP metadata and a SCIM token via our secure vault (will share via the doc link).
- No HSM for now — we use Azure Key Vault for signing. If Redwood needs HSM, we can open a procurement ticket but it will add lead time.
- IP ranges: staging 18.45.32.0/24, prod 18.45.64.0/24; we may need occasional maintenance windows where other IPs are allowed for short windows.
- Service accounts: we have two SRE leads who will own them (devops+procure cc'd). They prefer least-privilege and per-integration accounts.

Next steps: please share the service-account roster template and an example SCIM mapping you recommend; I'll validate with our identity team.

Tara

--
Tara Singh
Head of IT Operations, HelixHealth
tara@helixhealth.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Singh <tara@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: HelixHealth onboarding — access controls kickoff

Tara — thanks for the details. A few technical clarifications from our side:

1) SAML attributes: we'll need "email" and "groups" to be asserted. If you can include an immutable employee_id (or sub) that helps with deprovisioning.

2) SCIM: our recommended minimal mapping for HelixHealth roles:
   - okta.group: "redwood_admins" -> Redwood role: admin
   - okta.group: "redwood_users" -> Redwood role: user
   - okta.group: "redwood_billing" -> Redwood role: billing

   I'll attach a sample mapping snippet to the roster.

3) Service accounts: see below the proposed ownership model (quick summary):
   - per-integration SA (unique principal for each third-party integration)
   - short-lived tokens where possible (rotate every 30 days)
   - explicit owner (team lead) and audit owner (HelixHealth SRE)

I'm attaching the svc-account-roster.csv (stub) and the ip-allowlist-template.txt for your network team.

Question for Ben: when we ask for IP exceptions for maintenance windows, what's our recommended change window (duration + approval flow) and do we need Meraki firewall change tickets or is a HelixHealth managed change enough?

On the timeline, we can run the technical workshop on 11/23 at 14:00 PT if that works for DevOps.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-17T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: HelixHealth onboarding — access controls kickoff

Thanks — Jordan, thanks for the templates. Short answers on the network side:

- Recommended maintenance exception window: 2 hours by default (can be extended with 24h advance notice and approval). For our production SLOs we advise <= 4 hours; anything longer requires exec signoff.
- Approval flow: HelixHealth opens a change request to their network ops (we prefer the ticket), CC Redwood security@redwood.ai for audit; for emergency windows we accept verbal approval + a follow-up ticket within 24 hours.
- Firewall changes: HelixHealth-managed changes are fine as long as you provide the CIDR and a ticket ID; we will validate on our end once the change is live.

I've uploaded the attachments referenced to the shared folder and added a short implementation checklist to the plan. See Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcHelixOnboard

Action items:
- Jordan: finalize svc-account-roster.csv and add TTL/rotation policy column (owner: Jordan).
- Tara / DevOps: share IdP metadata & SCIM token in the shared folder and open a network change ticket for the staging range.
- Monica: schedule the 11/23 workshop and invite identity + SRE.

I'll prepare the firewall exception template and a short runbook for emergency approvals.

Cheers,
Ben
